name: AKKN density dichotomy (Dense Subset Sum may be the hardest)
description: Austrin-Kaski-Koivisto-Nederlof parameterize Subset Sum by the maximum bin size beta(w) = max_x |{S subset [n] : w(S)=x}|. They give a Monte Carlo algorithm that beats the 2^{n/2} meet-in-the-middle bound when beta <= 2^{(0.5-eps)n}, and a deterministic truly-faster algorithm when beta >= 2^{0.661n}. The gap 2^{0.5n} < beta < 2^{0.661n} is left open. Corollary: if density >= 1.003 instances are truly-faster solvable, so is everything.
authors_year_venue: P. Austrin, P. Kaski, M. Koivisto, J. Nederlof; STACS 2016 (venue per Randolph-Wegrzycki citation [AKKN16], pp. 13:1-13:14); arXiv:1508.06019. Companion: STACS 2015 'Subset sum in the absence of concentration' (time 2^{0.3399n} beta^4).
status_and_verification: Peer-reviewed (STACS 2016) per citation in arXiv 2407.18228; arXiv v1 read via alphaXiv: abstract, Sec 1 (all theorems), Sec 2 (Lemma 2.2), Sec 3 (Lemmas 3.1, 3.2, proofs of Thm 1.1, 1.2, start of 3.1), Sec 4 (Prop 4.2, 4.4 proof start), Sec 5-6. Not read: the tail of the Prop 4.4 proof (entropy calculation yielding 0.661). [uncertain]
key_theorem_or_bound: Thm 1.1: for 0<=eps<=1/6 there is a Monte Carlo algorithm solving all instances with beta(w) <= 2^{(0.5-eps)n} in O*(2^{(0.5 - eps/4 + 3eps^2/4)n}). Thm 1.2: exists delta>0 and a deterministic algorithm solving all instances with beta(w) >= 2^{0.661n} in O*(2^{(0.5-delta)n}). Lemma 1.3: |w(2^[n])| >= 2^{0.997n} implies beta <= 2^{0.4996n}. Lemma 1.4: if a balanced partition S,T has |w(2^S)|,|w(2^T)| >= 2^{(1/2-delta)n} then beta <= 2^{0.661n}. Prop 4.4: |w(2^S)| >= 2^{(1-delta)|S|} implies ||b_S||_2 <= 2^{0.661|S|}. Thm 1.5: |w(2^[n])| >= 2^{0.997n} solvable in O*(2^{0.49991n}).
regime_exponents: Small bins: beta <= 2^{(0.5-eps)n}, eps<=1/6 (time exponent 23/48 n at eps=1/6, about 0.479n). Large bins: beta >= 2^{0.661n}, 0.661 not claimed tight. Open window: 2^{0.5n} < beta < 2^{0.661n}. Meet-in-the-middle baseline 2^{n/2}. 0.311n (Howgrave-Graham-Joux random density-1) appears only as average-case context, and 0.2910n (Becker-Coron-Joux). Density threshold 1.003 from |w(2^[n])| >= 2^{0.997n}. D* thresholds are not treated in the paper.
proof_type_and_tools: Combinatorial/probabilistic plus information-theoretic. Lemma 3.1 merges Horowitz-Sahni meet-in-the-middle with the Howgrave-Graham-Joux representation technique on a block M with many sums (random prime p, second-moment/Cauchy-Schwarz collision count, Claim 2.1). Lemma 3.2: DP for blocks with few sums. Lemma 2.2: random-prime bit-length reduction preserving beta up to factor n. Combinatorial bounds via Uniquely Decodable Code Pairs (Prop 4.2, Ordentlich-Shayevitz Thm 4.3) and an l2 energy identity ||b||_2^2 = sum over y in {-1,0,1}^n with y.w=0 of 2^{#zeros(y)}.
quantitative_loss: Exponential and unoptimized: only the constant 0.661 and the eps/4 gain are proved; paper says constants are not tight and Lemma 1.3/1.4 are crude. Algorithm 1 has a naive bottleneck beta*2^{(1.5-gamma)mu n}. Gain over 2^{n/2} is 2^{-Omega(eps) n} for small bins, so it survives exponential-size bins (beta up to 2^{n/2}). The bound for beta in the middle window is not available.
worst_case_vs_average_case: Worst case over all inputs (Monte Carlo, no false positives); no randomness assumption on weights, unlike HGJ. Random density-2 instances have beta about 2^{0.5n}, so they sit in the unresolved window (paper remark).
coefficient_set: Plain {0,1} subset sums of n positive integers (bins count all subsets). The ||b||_2^2 identity introduces {-1,0,1} vectors y but only as an analysis device.
subset_size_regime: All subsets of [n]; bins are over every subset size. Lemma 3.1 conditions on |X cap M| = s, and its analysis uses subsets of size around |M|/2. No Theta(n)-size restriction on the bin itself; the 'old' paper conditions on solutions with n/2-size pairs (0.5254n remark).
relevance_to_Nc: Direct: ||b||_2^2 = sum_{U,V} [w(U)=w(V)] is the count of equal-sum pairs (collision energy), and the paper rewrites it as disjoint pairs weighted 2^{n-|U|-|V|}. So N_c (equal-sum disjoint pairs of Theta(n)-subsets) is a slice of ||b||_2^2, and beta >= 2^{0.661n} or beta <= 2^{(0.5-eps)n} are exactly the large-bin / small-bin outs of C1. Prop 4.4 bounds the energy by 2^{1.322|S|} when the half has near-full sums. Note beta controls only the maximum bin whereas N_c is a collision count; ||b||_2^2 <= beta * 2^n links them.
relevance_to_Dstar: Indirect. Lemma 1.4's hypothesis (both halves generate >= 2^{(1/2-delta)n} sums) is a lower bound on distinct half-sums, so the dichotomy says few distinct half-sums are exploitable (Lemma 3.2 with few sums gives time 2^{((1-mu(1-gamma))/2) n}). This is a D*-type threshold at 2^{(1/2-delta)n}, far above 2^{0.311n}; the paper gives no 2^{0.311n} statement. The relation D* <= 2^{0.311n} vs. hard instances is not proved here [uncertain].
applicability_gap: (1) Gap window beta in (2^{0.5n}, 2^{0.661n}) is unresolved, so C1's large-bin branch is only available above 0.661n. (2) Bins count subsets of all sizes, not disjoint equal-sum pairs of Theta(n)-subsets; passing from N_c to beta needs a pigeonhole/Cauchy-Schwarz step losing exponentials. (3) Large-bin algorithm is proved via partitions into halves with many sums, not via a fixed solution support (D*). (4) Constant 0.661 not tight; only improving past 0.5 is needed for the open question but improving 0.661 alone does not settle it (random density-2 inputs).
counterexample_or_hard_instance_family: Paper: random density-2 instance has beta about 2^{0.5n}; instance 1,1,3,3,9,9,27,27,... has |w(2^[n])| = 3^{n/2} and beta = 2^{n/2} (easy via Lemma 3.2). UDCP pairs with |A| >= 2^{(1-o(1))n} and |B| >= 2^{n/4} exist (Kasami et al.), so Lemma 1.3 route cannot give beta below 2^{n/4}.
dependency_chain: AKKN (small and large beta) -> Randolph-Wegrzycki worst-case representation (mixing dichotomy) for the intermediate regime -> BSG/energy for structure in large-energy case. Companion: Ordentlich-Shayevitz UDCP bounds; Howgrave-Graham-Joux representation technique.
constructiveness: Fully algorithmic: Theorem 1.1 is Monte Carlo, Theorem 1.2 deterministic; the combinatorial lemmas (1.3, 1.4) are existential bounds used only to pick which algorithm applies (case split guessed, not computed from beta). Cost is exponential 2^{(0.5-Omega(eps))n}. The algorithm does not need to know beta; it tries each block.
lean_formalizable: Moderate for Prop 4.2 (UDCP from injective set plus a bin) and the l2 energy identity in a mathlib-free setting; hard for Theorem 4.3 (Ordentlich-Shayevitz) and the entropy calculation of 0.661, which need analytic estimates.
computational_check: Source has no experiments (theory paper). Repo could brute-force beta, |w(2^[n])| and ||b||_2^2 for n <= 40 (2^n subset-sum enumeration is borderline at n=40 but fine at n<=30) via the existing scripts/analysis style, to see where random/structured instances fall relative to 0.5n and 0.661n.
next_experiment: Compute log2 beta/n and log2 ||b||_2^2 / n for random density 1,1.5,2 and for GAP/rank-d instances at n<=30, and record the ratio of N_c (disjoint equal-sum pairs of size-cn subsets) to ||b||_2^2 to quantify the slice loss when passing between C1 and Prop 4.4.
open_issues: Open Question 3 of the paper: if |w(2^[n])| >= 2^{(1-eps)n}, are beta <= 2^{o_eps(1)n} and ||b||_2 <= 2^{(0.5+o(1))n}? The middle window is unresolved; a previous version used an extra pair-count bound 2^{0.5254n} not retained. Lemma 6.1 (beta <= 2^{0.4115n} when |A| >= 2^{(1-delta)n}) is cited as unpublished.
